This applies to any Fell that went to the shaft. Any Fell who went to the river door is in [[03 - The Larders|The Larders]] or [[04 - The River Door|The River Door]].

> [!reminder] How this scene works
> The Fell crawl down Nib's shaft with stone. Three things happen here.
> - **Stone.** The stone heap is at the top hole. Each Fell who stays at the top before going down may lower one load on the rope, one Bearing roll each, and every load that lands is one fewer they need in the fight below. Work out the stone needed when they reach the bottom: 2, plus the segments filled on the floor clock.
> - **Two places.** The top hole is where the shaft starts, in the floor of the lower tunnels. The opening is where the shaft comes out at the bottom, into the hollow. The stone is set across the opening.
> - **The weasels.** At the bottom, weasels the root has caught come out of the walls. They want warmth, and nothing else: lamps and bodies. The Fell can get past them without a fight, by going dark and still, or by sending a lit lamp up a side tunnel for them to follow. Both are written below. If they fight, it is a short one.
> - **Nib's mark.** The clay plug the root broke through has Nib's sign on it. That is the clue to her secret.
> Then the root opens its eyes, and scene 6 starts at once.

> [!readaloud] Opening: The lower tunnels
> The stairs go down into the lower tunnels, which are low enough that you walk bent double. The floor here is cracked across in a dozen places, and through every crack shows grey. At the end of the last tunnel, in the floor, is a round hole about as wide as your shoulders, with a ladder going down into it and a rope tied off to an iron ring. Beside it is a heap of cut stones and a trough of mortar. The air coming up out of the hole is warm and wet and smells of rotten wood.

**This applies to any Fell who arrives after the floor clock reached 1 or more.** Read the cracked floor as worse: the grey is showing through the flagstones in long seams, and it moves when no one is looking at it.

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If she came with them, or from halfway down the ladder if she didn't:* "Here's how it goes. At the bottom it opens out into a hollow, and the root's in the hollow, coming up. We drop stone down on the rope, and we wall the shaft off across the bottom where it opens out, with mortar, proper, a good tight course. How much stone depends how far it's come. It was two loads this morning. It goes up every time that floor moves."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If asked how she knows what's at the bottom:* "Because I looked. Earlier. Come on."

> [!reminder] Stone
> Write the stone needed down now: 2, plus the segments filled on the floor clock. Before going down, each Fell may stay at the top long enough to lower one load: one Bearing roll each, once. Loads that land wait at the bottom by the opening, ready to set in the next scene.

> [!lorecheck] Movement: The crawl
> Every Fell who goes down rolls Movement, or Elusion if they choose to squeeze rather than climb. A Shrewish Fell does not roll. The shaft was dug for them, and they go down it easily.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You go down the ladder, then off it where the shaft bends, flat on your belly through the clay, and you come out the bottom first with a lamp in your teeth. *Then:* This Fell reaches the bottom first and sees the hollow before anything in it sees them. Their Movement increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* It's tight and warm and it smells awful, and the bend nearly has you, but you come out at the bottom.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You stick fast at the bend. Your shoulders are wedged in the clay and the lamp is somewhere behind you. It takes a lot of wriggling to come loose. *Then:* This Fell reaches the bottom last.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You stick at the bend and the clay gives way under you. You slide the rest of the way down on your back and land in a heap at the bottom, in the dark, in something soft. *Then:* This Fell reaches the bottom last, and lands right next to the weasels.

> [!lorecheck] Bearing: Bringing stone
> Each Fell who lowers a load before going down rolls once.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You lower two stones at once on the rope, slow and smooth, and they land at the bottom without a crack. *Then:* Two loads at the bottom. Their Bearing increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The rope bites into your hands, and the stone goes down, and lands. *Then:* One load at the bottom.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* The stone swings and catches on the bend and won't go further. You haul it back up and start again.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* The rope slips. The stone goes down the shaft by itself, and from the bottom comes a long crunch. *Then:* The stone breaks at the bottom. No load. This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!readaloud] The hollow
> At the bottom the shaft opens into a hollow in the clay, wider than the great hall upstairs and much lower, the roof just over your head. Water drips. Your lamp shows clay walls, then grey. Most of the far wall is root. It is a single root, grey and soft and as big around as a house, and it fills the far side of the hollow and goes up into the dark. It is moving, slowly, rising and settling. The shaft you came down is right above it.

> [!lorecheck] Vigilance: The walls
> Any Fell at the bottom who looks around.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* The clay walls are full of holes, round and small, and something is moving in all of them at once. Thin grey shapes, long-bodied, wound round and round with soft bark. Weasels, or what's left of them. Their heads all turn your way together. *Then:* This Fell sees them before they move. Their Vigilance increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* Something is moving in the holes in the walls. Long, thin, grey.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* Clay and root and dark. Nothing else.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You're looking the wrong way, at the big root, when something grey and thin drops off the wall right beside your face. *Then:* This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!readaloud] Rootbound weasels
> They come out of the walls all together. Weasels, long-bodied and low, but wound in soft grey bark from nose to tail, so they bulge in the wrong places. Their eyes are open and blank. They move all at once and too smoothly, every one of them turning the same way at the same time, and none of them makes a sound.

> [!lorecheck] Lore: Rootbound beasts
> Any Fell who knows them.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* A rotted root grows over anything warm and walks it about. What it catches it keeps, wound in bark. The Shrewish call them rootbound. These were weasels. They aren't now. The root moves them, and nothing else does. *Then:* Their Lore increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* Rootbound. Animals the grey root caught and wound in bark, and now moves.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You've never seen anything like them.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You're certain they're asleep and won't wake if you keep quiet. They're already moving.

> [!reminder] Getting past the weasels without a fight
> The weasels go for warmth and light. Any Fell may try one of these as the weasels come out of the walls.
> - **Go dark.** Every lamp out, and every Fell holds still in the dark. One Fell rolls Poise for the group.
> - **Lure them.** Set a lit lamp in the mouth of one of the side holes and push it in. One Fell rolls Trickery.
> If either works, the weasels pour away after the lamp or lose the Fell in the dark, and there is no fight here. They come back in scene 6, drawn by the light the Fell need to set stone. If both fail, or the Fell choose to fight, run the crucible below.

> [!lorecheck] Poise: Going dark
> The Fell who calls it, for everyone at the bottom.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You put the lamp out and stand still. In the dark you hear them come right up to you, a dry slither across the clay, and stop. Then they turn, every one at once, and slide away back into the walls. *Then:* No fight. Their Poise increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* Lamps out. You hold your breath. Something brushes past your boot and keeps going. *Then:* No fight.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* Somebody shifts their weight. The weasels turn toward the sound together. *Then:* Run the crucible.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You knock the lamp over as you reach for it, and the oil runs across the clay, burning. Every weasel in the walls turns toward the fire, and toward you. *Then:* Run the crucible. This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!lorecheck] Trickery: The lamp in the side tunnel
> The Fell who sets the lamp.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You set the lamp in a side hole and nudge it along with your boot until it rolls away down the slope inside. Every weasel in the hollow turns and goes after it, in one long grey line. *Then:* No fight. Their Trickery increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* The lamp goes in and the weasels go after it. *Then:* No fight.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* The lamp goes in a hand's length and sticks. Half the weasels go for it. The other half keep coming for you. *Then:* Run the crucible.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* The lamp tips back out onto your feet. *Then:* Run the crucible. This Fell is at the shaft, so the floor clock fills one segment.

> [!crucible] The weasels
> The [[Rootbound Weasel]]s come out of the walls. One per Fell at the bottom. Each has 4 Vitality and only its Standard Attack. Run it short, two or three rounds. Spend no Disruptions. The big root does not take part in this fight. It moves a little each round, and that is all.

## Nib at the bottom

This applies if Nib came down with the Fell, or is already at the bottom. She is not in the fight. She mixes mortar in a bucket by the opening and keeps her head down, and the weasels ignore her because she has no lamp. No foe targets her, and she cannot fall.

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *Mid-fight, stirring mortar:* "Don't mind me. Keep them off the stone. That's all I'm asking."

## Closing the fight

This applies to every Fell at the bottom, whether they fought or got past the weasels by a roll. Weasels got past by a roll count as defeated.

> [!reminder] Closing the battle
> Close the fight in this order. Name every foe the Fell defeated. Then the Fatigue check: you roll 1d6 + 0 once for the table, and each Fell rolls 1d6 + Endurance against it. Then the [[Treasure Phase]]: every Fell who rolled a Fellmark or was granted Luck since their last rest or the end of their last battle takes a Treasure Roll. Lore Points come last. The weasels pay 1 Lore Point.

> [!clue] Nib's sign
> In the clay around the opening, where the plug used to be, there are tool marks. The marks are neat and square, from a narrow chisel. Cut into the clay beside them is a small sign: a circle with a line through it. Any Fell who was in the great hall saw that sign carved over the river arch, and on the door of the store room, and on Nib's apron buckle. It is her mark. She puts it on everything she builds.

> [!readaloud] Closing: The eyes on the root
> The hollow is quiet except for the dripping. If you fought, the weasels lie still on the clay, and the bark around them has gone loose, with something small and long dead inside. Then the big root moves. It is a long slow push upward, and the clay under your feet shifts with it, and up the shaft, far above you, you hear the warren groan. Something on the root opens its eyes. They are flat and round, and they catch your lamplight and give none of it back.

> [!beat] Where everyone is now
> Every Fell at the bottom goes straight into [[06 - The Grey Mother|The Grey Mother]]. Any Fell still at the top lowering stone may come down now or keep lowering. Say where each one is.
